title: Alias-collision refusal cannot say WHAT holds the colliding key, because occupied[] discards the owner and the id-vs-alias distinction at construction
description:
Routed by opum-agent 2026-09-19 (new session, OPAG-321) after opum-doc caught that OPAG-253 mis-cites this as "filed QCLI-353". The mis-citation is real and confirmed: QCLI-353 is the task-create positional-title flag-swallowing gap, unrelated to migration. So this genuinely was never filed.

BUT THE ASK AS ROUTED IS MOSTLY ALREADY SHIPPED, and the scope below is narrowed accordingly rather than filed as received.

The routed request asked for the message to name the colliding key, name which of the two collision shapes it is, and say so explicitly when the two are indistinguishable. All three already exist. QCLI-167 (Done, 2026-09-02) added the cause-agnostic hint, and a fleet-reported enrichment on 2026-09-09 added the second cause and its remedy. The live message, read at src/application/migration/backlog-public.ts:520-522 and pinned verbatim by a passing test at test/e2e/migration/backlog-public.test.ts:741, is:

  Alias collision: "qcli-1" conflicts with "QCLI-1". If this is from positional
  renumbering (for example a dotted subtask flattening and shifting a later
  allocation), --preserve-source-ids --source-family <PREFIX> avoids it by keeping
  each record own source id instead. If instead this exact id is already a live,
  unrelated claim in the destination workspace, --preserve-source-ids will not
  resolve it -- rename or remove the conflicting record in the destination, or
  rename the id in the source, before retrying.

It names the key, names BOTH shapes, states that it cannot tell them apart, and gives a remedy for each. Verified by running the suite: 11 pass, 0 fail.

WHY THE ROUTED DESCRIPTION SAID OTHERWISE. It describes the bare "Alias collision: OPAG-2 conflicts with OPAG-2" with no hint -- which is precisely the pre-QCLI-167 message, quoted in QCLI-167 own description from the 2026-09-02 report. OPAG-253 recorded the defect accurately when it was written and was read seventeen days later as a present-tense description. The structural claims relayed alongside it were all verified correct here (assertAliasesAvailable at :505 sits in previewInternal default branch; :465 early-returns into previewWithPreservedIds when preserveSourceIds is set; the comment above it is deliberately cause-agnostic). So the relay was accurate about the CODE and stale about the MESSAGE, and only re-reading the message could tell them apart.

THE GENUINE RESIDUAL GAP, which is the one thing asked for that is NOT implemented. The request also asked the message to name "what already holds it -- destination task id vs registered alias". It does not, and it currently cannot. occupied is built at :461-464 as

  const occupied: Alias[] = existing.taskRecords.flatMap((entry) => [
    alias(entry.task.id),
    ...entry.task.aliases.map(alias),
  ]);

which flattens both kinds into one Alias[] and keeps neither the owning task nor whether the entry came from the canonical id or from the alias list. By the time assertAliasesAvailable throws at :505 that provenance is gone, so the message can only print the key twice -- and when the two sides render as the same string, which is the common case, an operator has nothing to act on. The information exists at :461 and is discarded one line later.

So this is a PLUMBING task, not a wording task: carry the owner and the kind alongside each occupied entry, and have the refusal say "X is already the canonical id of TASK-N" or "X is already a registered alias of TASK-N". Note assertAliasesAvailable lives in src/domain/records.ts:106 and is shared, so the shape change is not local to migration -- collectAliasCollisions alongside it has the same signature.

PRIORITY SET TO LOW, DEPARTING FROM THE ROUTED SUGGESTION OF MEDIUM, and the reason matters more than the value. The routed justification was that this "has now cost two sessions a wrong diagnosis and one mis-citation". Those costs are real but they were caused by OPAG-253 stale record, not by the live message -- neither session hit the collision. The genuine residual gap has no reported operator victim at all. Raising it is fine if someone hits it; inheriting a priority from evidence that belongs to a different defect is not.

THE INVARIANT IS NOT IN QUESTION. opum-agent has ruled KEEP on the check and opum-doc is landing that record. Quest holds one global id+alias index, a second claim throws dependency_target_ambiguous, and the alternative to refusing up front is silent misrouting. Nothing here proposes relaxing it.

acceptanceCriteria.text: An alias-collision refusal names what already holds the colliding key -- the owning task, and whether the key is that task canonical id or one of its registered aliases -- rather than printing the same string on both sides
The refusal keeps the two cause-shapes and both remedies it already carries, verified by the existing verbatim-message test being updated deliberately rather than deleted
The added provenance is carried from where it is known (the occupied construction) rather than re-derived at the throw site by a second read of the repository
collectAliasCollisions is considered in the same change, since it shares assertAliasesAvailable signature in src/domain/records.ts and would otherwise diverge
A regression test covers both occupant kinds -- a collision against a canonical id and a collision against a registered alias -- and asserts the message distinguishes them
